newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra discussing air beyond rights with NZ.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra discussing air beyond rights with NZ.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Thursday negotiations over the possibility of granting New Zealand airlines the right to fly beyond Australia had started following the creation of a single aviation market.
"We are very aware of the interest that New Zealand has in this and we are now in a process of negotiating with the New Zealand government over beyond rights," Sharp told reporters.

Sharp earlier confirmed the establishment of a single trans-Tasman aviation market from November 1 this year, under which the airlines of both countries would have unrestricted rights to fly anywhere in the other country.

However, the agreement did not include beyond rights for New Zealand airlines unlike an earlier proposal, which former Labor Party government transport minister Laurie Brereton cancelled shortly before it was to come into effect two years ago.
Sharp said the negotiations would hinge on formal consultation with Australian air operators as well as the New Zealand government.
Asked when a decision on the issue was likely, Sharp said: "It will depend on our discussions with our own operators, but I'm hopeful that we can do this sooner rather than later."
